app_info.subtitle: Pay-per-use APIs for agents
app_info.description: Locus gives an agent one prepaid credit balance for its paid work: cited web research, data and API lookups from a contracted provider catalog, executable cost quotes, and idempotent billing - a retry that reuses its idempotency key replays the stored outcome instead of charging again. The agent searches the catalog in plain English, inspects one endpoint's schema and price, optionally locks an exact quote, and executes by slug; every charge returns the exact credits debited and the remaining balance, and workspace owners control spend limits and approvals from the Locus dashboard.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only queries the enabled catalog index and returns ranked matches with slugs and prices; it cannot execute, enable, or modify anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: Searches Locus's own catalog index and contacts no external services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Returns search results only and changes no state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns only categories and curated packs already executable for the authenticated connection; it cannot enable tools or change permissions.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads the scoped Locus catalog registry only and contacts no external provider.
justifications.destructive_justification: Returns discovery metadata only and changes no state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns immutable public Locus guidance and supporting resource identifiers without changing account state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the deployed Locus guide bundle and contacts no provider.
justifications.destructive_justification: Guide retrieval is read-only and cannot install software, authorize spend, or publish customer content.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns one endpoint's input schema, example, output shape, and price without invoking it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads Locus catalog metadata only; no external calls.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a bounded page of the connection's enabled endpoints without invoking any of them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads the Locus catalog only; no external calls.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the authenticated connection's remaining credit balance and status.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads Locus ledger state only; no external calls.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reads a balance and changes no state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Re-reads a bounded chunk of a previously stored call result by its receipt ID without re-running the call.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads stored results from Locus only; no external calls.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reads a stored result and never creates a new charge.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a short-lived executable price approval on the server, so it is not purely a read, but it never charges credits.
justifications.open_world_justification: May probe a live upstream quote to price a variable-cost endpoint exactly, without paying it.
justifications.destructive_justification: Never charges or removes anything; an unused approval simply expires.

justifications.read_only_justification: Invalidates a stored price approval, which is a state change rather than a read.
justifications.open_world_justification: Acts on Locus-stored approvals only; no external calls.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently invalidates the referenced unused approval so it can no longer authorize an execution; no credits are involved.

justifications.read_only_justification: Spends prepaid credits and runs the selected endpoint, so it is a billed action rather than a read.
justifications.open_world_justification: Invokes external provider APIs from the Locus catalog and returns their responses.
justifications.destructive_justification: Debits credits from the prepaid balance for each non-replayed call; retries with the same idempotency key replay the stored outcome instead of charging again.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates or revises tenant-private Workflow drafts and saves checked immutable versions, so the combined action tool can change Locus state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Stores and reads Workflow source inside Locus only and does not contact external providers.
justifications.destructive_justification: Draft revisions and immutable saves do not delete external data, spend credits, publish, or schedule execution.

justifications.read_only_justification: Persists validation evidence and may start an isolated fixture sandbox, so it is not a pure read.
justifications.open_world_justification: Structural checks do not execute code; fixture mode blocks outbound network and carries no live provider authority.
justifications.destructive_justification: Validation records evidence only and cannot dispatch a paid provider call or modify external data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Queues a hosted Workflow that can perform multiple billed Locus calls under a hard run ceiling.
justifications.open_world_justification: The isolated run may invoke only its saved, currently authorized external Locus bindings through the execution gateway.
justifications.destructive_justification: A new run can debit prepaid credits; a replayed idempotency key returns the existing run instead of starting another.

justifications.read_only_justification: The combined action tool can inspect, cancel, or resume a durable run, so it is not always read-only.
justifications.open_world_justification: Run control reads and changes Locus control-plane state; provider calls happen only inside a separately authorized run.
justifications.destructive_justification: Cancel permanently blocks new dispatch for the current attempt, while resume can continue eligible unfinished work and spend the remaining authorized budget.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs a billed multi-provider web search, so it is a paid action rather than a read.
justifications.open_world_justification: Dispatches to external search providers from the Locus catalog and returns normalized results.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves search results and bills credits for them; it modifies or deletes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs a billed research workflow that may execute catalog capabilities, so it is a paid action rather than a read.
justifications.open_world_justification: Selects and calls external catalog capabilities to produce a cited answer.
justifications.destructive_justification: Produces research output and bills credits for the underlying calls; it modifies or deletes nothing.

test_cases.description: Discover a capability by outcome: the user asks for an API that can do a job, and the app searches the enabled catalog and returns ranked, priced matches. Fixture: the provided demo workspace reached through the app's OAuth sign-in with the demo credentials - funded prepaid balance, default 1,000-credits-per-dollar denomination, exa/answer and brave/answers enabled, capability routing on.
test_cases.user_prompt: Find me an API through Locus that can answer research questions with cited sources, and tell me what each option costs.
test_cases.expected_output: A short ranked list of catalog matches (including exa/answer and brave/answers) with each endpoint's slug, one-line summary, and credit price.

test_cases.description: Inspect one endpoint before calling it: the user asks for the input schema and price of a specific slug. Fixture: the provided demo workspace reached through the app's OAuth sign-in with the demo credentials - funded prepaid balance, default 1,000-credits-per-dollar denomination, exa/answer and brave/answers enabled, capability routing on.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the input schema, an example call, and the exact price for the exa/answer endpoint on Locus.
test_cases.expected_output: The endpoint's input schema (a required query string), an example invocation, its output shape, and the fixed price of 8 credits (~$0.008).

test_cases.description: Check remaining prepaid credits: the user asks for the balance before doing paid work. Fixture: the provided demo workspace reached through the app's OAuth sign-in with the demo credentials - funded prepaid balance, default 1,000-credits-per-dollar denomination, exa/answer and brave/answers enabled, capability routing on.
test_cases.user_prompt: How many Locus credits do I have left on this workspace?
test_cases.expected_output: The current credit balance with its denomination (1 credit = $0.001) and active status, with no charge made.

test_cases.description: Quote without spending: the user names the endpoint and the exact request body, wants a binding price, explicitly does not want the call executed, and asks for the quote to be released. The app reads the schema, quotes those arguments, and cancels the unused approval. Fixture: the provided demo workspace reached through the app's OAuth sign-in with the demo credentials - funded prepaid balance, default 1,000-credits-per-dollar denomination, exa/answer and brave/answers enabled, capability routing on.
test_cases.user_prompt: On Locus, look up the exa/answer endpoint's schema, then quote exactly what a call with the body {"query": "what is the x402 payment protocol"} would cost. Do not run it, and cancel the quote when you have the number.
test_cases.expected_output: A binding quote of 8 credits with an approval reference, followed by confirmation the approval was cancelled; the balance is unchanged.

test_cases.description: End-to-end paid call with an explicit slug and arguments: the user names the endpoint, the app confirms it in the catalog and its price, executes it with the given query, cites the sources, and reports the exact charge and remaining balance. Fixture: the provided demo workspace reached through the app's OAuth sign-in with the demo credentials - funded prepaid balance, default 1,000-credits-per-dollar denomination, exa/answer and brave/answers enabled, capability routing on.
test_cases.user_prompt: On Locus, find the exa/answer endpoint, confirm its price, then run it with the query "what is the x402 payment protocol" and give me the cited answer plus exactly what it charged.
test_cases.expected_output: A synthesized answer with source citations, the exact charge of 8 credits from the response metadata, and the remaining balance.

test_cases.description: Create a repeatable process without local files: the execute-capable staging connection exposes hosted Workflows and deterministic fixtures for the approved demo capability.
test_cases.user_prompt: Using Locus, turn a two-company research task into a reusable Workflow, check it, test fixtures, save version 1, and queue a pilot capped at 20 credits. Do not schedule or publish it.
test_cases.tools_triggered: get_locus_guide, search_apis, describe_api, workflow_definition, workflow_validate, workflow_run, workflow_runs
test_cases.expected_output: A tenant-private checked Workflow version and bounded pilot run ID, followed by durable status, exact charge/receipt evidence, and no new agent connection, schedule, or publication.

negative_test_cases.description: A documentation question about the app itself should be answered from knowledge, not by invoking catalog tools or spending credits.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Explain how the Locus app works and what its tools are for.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because this is a documentation question rather than a request to use its tools.

negative_test_cases.description: Account administration is not exposed through these tools; the app should direct the user to the Locus dashboard instead of attempting it.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Change my Locus account password and update the billing email on my workspace.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because account administration is outside its exposed tool workflows.

negative_test_cases.description: Purchasing credits is not available through the app; the app should decline and point to the workspace dashboard rather than initiate any purchase or checkout flow.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Buy $50 of Locus credits for me right now.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because purchasing credits is not available through its tools.
